concepts.name: Users of accounting information and their needs
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Owners, managers, employees, investors, lenders, suppliers, customers, government (tax authority) and public and environmental bodies: what each wants to know and which statement or ratio answers it; how information is communicated to each group (internal management reports against published statements); qualitative characteristics in words (relevance, reliability, comparability, understandability) without the IFRS Conceptual Framework detail. Ratios themselves are aacc.ratios.*.

concepts.name: Types of business organisation: sole trader, partnership, company
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Sole trader, partnership, private and public limited company (plc) compared on legal form, ownership, control, liability, continuity, raising capital, taxation and disclosure; advantages and disadvantages of each from the owners' and other stakeholders' view; ZIMSEC detail: formal and non-formal (informal) organisations, small-to-medium enterprises and large businesses in Zimbabwe. Choosing a structure for a described business. Limited liability partnerships are not examined. Sources of finance are aacc.capital.*.

concepts.name: Branches of accounting
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). ZIMSEC detail: financial accounting, financial reporting, cost accounting and management accounting: purpose, users, who prepares each and how they differ (statutory against internal, past against future, rules against flexibility); where bookkeeping, auditing and taxation fit. No calculations beyond examples of typical outputs.

concepts.name: Business ethics and professional ethics for accountants
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). The need for an ethical framework; the fundamental principles of integrity, objectivity, professional competence and due care, confidentiality and professional behaviour; threats (self-interest, familiarity, intimidation, pressure to manipulate figures, conflict of interest) and safeguards; ethical dilemmas in recording, reporting and tax; how the behaviour of accountants and auditors affects the business and stakeholders; social implications of decisions; applying business ethics in day-to-day transactions (ZIMSEC), with Unhu/Ubuntu values as context. No named codes of conduct or legal cases.

concepts.name: Sources of finance for sole traders, partnerships and companies
concepts.description: Cambridge only (AS Level). Cambridge detail: secured and unsecured loans, bank overdrafts, payment by instalments, renting and leasing as an alternative to purchase, trade credit: the cost, security, repayment and risk of each and which suits a described need (working capital against non-current assets); matching source to purpose and to type of entity. Share and loan-note finance is aacc.capital.sources-of-capital.

concepts.name: Long-term capital: shares, loan notes and their advantages and disadvantages
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Ordinary shares, preference shares (redeemable and irredeemable), loan notes/debentures (secured, unsecured, redeemable, irredeemable) and convertible loan stock; advantages and disadvantages to the company and to the investor of issuing shares against loan notes, of bonus and rights issues, retained earnings as a source; effect on gearing, control and dividends; choosing finance for a stated purpose. Preference shares and convertible loan stock are ZIMSEC detail (Cambridge sets no questions on preference shares). Accounting entries are aacc.company.*.

concepts.name: Concepts of recording: entity, historical cost, money measurement, duality, objectivity
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Business entity, historical cost convention (and why it is questioned), money measurement and its limits, duality (double entry), objectivity (evidence), with applications: private expenses, inflation, goodwill and staff skills not recorded. Applying each concept to a described situation and naming the concept breached. Prudence, matching, realisation, materiality, consistency, going concern and substance over form are aacc.concepts.reporting.

concepts.name: Concepts of reporting: prudence, matching, realisation, materiality, consistency, going concern, substance over form
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Prudence (no overstating profit or assets), realisation (revenue recognised when earned, not when paid), matching/accruals, materiality, consistency, going concern (and what changes if it fails) and substance over form (finance leases, sale and repurchase), each with worked applications to inventory, depreciation, accruals, allowances and disclosure; identifying the concept behind a treatment and the effect on profit and assets. Recording concepts are aacc.concepts.recording.

concepts.name: Double entry, the accounting equation and ledger accounts
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Duality: every transaction affects two accounts; debit and credit rules for assets, liabilities, capital, income and expenses; the accounting equation A = C + L and its use to analyse transactions; ledger accounts (T and running-balance formats), balancing off, capital and drawings accounts, returns, carriage and discounts, taken from the Principles of Accounting prerequisite but at A-Level pace; bringing down balances and distinguishing debit from credit balances. Books of prime entry are aacc.ledger.books-prime-entry; the trial balance is aacc.ledger.trial-balance.

concepts.name: Books of prime entry and the general journal
concepts.description: Cambridge only (AS Level). Cambridge detail: sales journal, sales returns journal, purchases journal, purchases returns journal, cash book (with discounts) and the general journal: what goes into each, source documents, posting to the sales and purchases ledgers and the general ledger, control-account totals; journal entries for opening entries, purchase and sale of non-current assets on credit, correction of errors and write-offs; advantages and disadvantages of maintaining full accounting records. No folio columns.

concepts.name: Accruals and prepayments of expenses and income in the ledger
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Ledger accounts for expenses and income with accrued and prepaid amounts (rent, rates, insurance, wages, interest, commission received), carried-down and brought-down balances, transfer to the statement of profit or loss, reversal at the start of the next period; the matching concept; effect on profit and on the statement of financial position. Presenting them in the statements is aacc.statements.adjustments.

concepts.name: Irrecoverable (bad) debts, recoveries and allowances for doubtful debts
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Writing off an irrecoverable (bad) debt, irrecoverable debts recovered, creating, increasing and reducing an allowance for irrecoverable (doubtful) debts as a percentage of trade receivables, the allowance account and the charge or credit to profit or loss, statement of financial position presentation (receivables less allowance); the prudence concept. Terminology: ZIMSEC bad debts and allowances for doubtful debts; Cambridge irrecoverable debts and allowance for irrecoverable debts.

concepts.name: Capital and revenue expenditure and income
concepts.description: Cambridge only (AS Level). Cambridge detail: capital expenditure (acquiring or improving non-current assets) against revenue expenditure (running costs and repairs), capital against revenue income; mixed items (installation, legal fees on purchase, repairs and improvement); the effect on profit and on asset value of misclassifying (overstated or understated profit, asset values, depreciation); journal entries correcting a misclassification. Depreciation is aacc.ledger.depreciation.

concepts.name: Depreciation: causes, methods and provision for depreciation accounts
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Why non-current assets lose value (wear, time, obsolescence, depletion, legal limits) and why depreciation is charged (matching, prudence, fair profit); straight-line and reducing-balance calculations with residual value and part-year rules stated by the question; choosing the more appropriate method; non-current asset, provision for depreciation (accumulated depreciation) and depreciation expense accounts; the charge in the statement of profit or loss and the carrying amount in the statement of financial position. Disposals are aacc.ledger.nca-disposal.

concepts.name: Disposal of non-current assets
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Disposal account method: transfer of cost and accumulated depreciation, proceeds, profit or loss on disposal and its place in the statement of profit or loss; part exchange (the allowance is the proceeds; the new asset is recorded at cost); disposal during the year with depreciation to the date of sale as the question states; journal entries; disposal of assets bought on credit or sold on credit. Revaluation entries are aacc.valuation.nca-models.

concepts.name: The trial balance: preparation, purpose, benefits and limitations
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Extracting balances from the ledger into debit and credit columns, the totals agreeing, what an agreeing trial balance proves and does not prove, locating a difference (casting, transposition, one-sided entry), the trial balance as the starting point for final accounts, accounts with debit and credit balances classified (assets, expenses, drawings against liabilities, income, capital); preparing a trial balance from ledger balances or a list. Types of error are aacc.verification.errors.

concepts.name: Inventory valuation: IAS 2, lower of cost and net realisable value, FIFO and AVCO
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). IAS 2: inventory measured at the lower of cost and net realisable value (item by item), what is included in cost, net realisable value calculations with selling costs, adjusting closing inventory in the final accounts; FIFO and weighted average cost (AVCO) under both the perpetual (after each transaction) and periodic (at the end of the period) systems, stores ledger records, effect of rising and falling prices on cost of sales and profit; inventory counted after the year end (roll back or forward). Just in time is aacc.cost.materials-labour-jit; LIFO is not examined.

concepts.name: Non-current asset valuation: IAS 16, cost model and revaluation model
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). IAS 16 recognition and measurement (cost, subsequent expenditure), the cost model against the revaluation model, revaluation upwards (revaluation reserve, a capital reserve) and the effect on depreciation, downward revaluation, valuation bases (historical cost, replacement cost, net realisable/exit value) compared and when each is useful; ledger accounts and journal entries for acquisition and revaluation; presentation in the statement of financial position and statement of changes in equity. Impairment and intangibles are aacc.standards.ias-16-36-38. The revaluation reserve is not used for bonus issues.

concepts.name: Reconciliation and verification of ledger accounts
concepts.description: Cambridge only (AS Level). Cambridge detail: why ledger accounts are reconciled and verified with internal documents (invoices, credit notes, delivery notes, goods received notes, inventory records) and external documents (supplier and bank statements, third-party confirmations); the benefits and limitations of each procedure (errors that persist, reliance on third parties, timing differences, cost) and who checks. The procedures themselves are aacc.verification.bank-reconciliation and aacc.verification.control-accounts.

concepts.name: Errors: those revealed and not revealed by the trial balance
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Errors of omission, commission, principle, original entry, reversal and compensating errors (no effect on the trial balance) against one-sided entries, wrong amounts on one side, and addition errors (which affect it); identifying, classifying and correcting by journal; the effect of each error on gross profit, profit for the year and working capital. The suspense account and corrected trial balance are aacc.verification.suspense.

concepts.name: Suspense accounts, corrected trial balances and corrected profit
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Opening a suspense account for a trial balance difference, journal entries that correct errors through suspense, preparing the suspense account to closure, drawing up a corrected trial balance, statements of corrected profit (gross profit, net profit/loss for the year) and corrected working capital starting from the draft figures, the effect on the statement of financial position; ZIMSEC calls these corrected net profit or loss. Error types are aacc.verification.errors.

concepts.name: Control accounts and personal ledger reconciliation
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Sales ledger and purchases ledger control accounts: the entries (credit sales, returns, receipts, discounts allowed/received, irrecoverable debts, contra entries, dishonoured cheques, interest charged), preparing them from totals of books of prime entry, adjusting the control account and the personal ledger for errors, reconciling the list of personal balances to the control account, what a control account does and does not detect, benefits and limitations; the effect of corrections on the financial statements.

concepts.name: Updated cash book and bank reconciliation statements
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Differences between the cash book and the bank statement: unpresented cheques, outstanding lodgements, bank charges, interest, direct debits and credits, standing orders, dishonoured cheques, errors by either party; updating the cash book; preparing a bank reconciliation statement from either balance; treatment of an overdrawn balance; correcting errors in the cash book and on the bank statement; effect on the statement of financial position; benefits and limitations.

concepts.name: Computerised accounting systems: use, advantages, disadvantages and data security
concepts.description: Cambridge only (AS Level). Cambridge detail: using a computerised system to record transactions and prepare reports (ledgers, trial balance, statements, ratios), advantages and disadvantages against a manual system (speed, accuracy, cost, training, dependence, hacking, system failure), and ways to secure data (passwords and access levels, backups, encryption, firewalls and anti-virus, audit trails, physical security). No specific software. ZIMSEC lists ICT tools only as a resource, so this is not a ZIMSEC syllabus topic.

concepts.name: Transferring manual accounts to a computerised system
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only). Cambridge detail (A Level): the process of changing over (planning, cleansing the data, opening balances and trial balance, parallel running, direct and phased changeover), ways to ensure the integrity of the data in transfer (control totals, trial balance agreement, reconciliations, validation and verification checks, testing and sign-off), risks and costs. No specific software.

concepts.name: Year-end adjustments to the draft financial statements
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Applying accruals and prepayments of expenses and income, depreciation, irrecoverable debts and recoveries, allowances for irrecoverable debts, closing inventory, goods taken by the owner and correction of errors to a trial balance when preparing the statements; the effect of each adjustment on profit and on assets and liabilities; extended-trial-balance (worksheet) layout; the matching/accruals concept. Ledger entries for the individual adjustments are in aacc.ledger.*.

concepts.name: Final accounts of a sole trader (trading and service businesses)
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Statement of profit or loss (revenue, cost of sales with carriage inwards, returns and discounts, gross profit, other income, expenses, profit for the year) and statement of financial position (non-current assets at carrying amount, current assets, current liabilities, working capital, capital plus profit less drawings) for a sole trader from a trial balance and adjustments; a service business has no cost of sales; IAS 1 format (Cambridge Teacher Guidance), income statement and trading account in ZIMSEC usage. Incomplete records are aacc.incomplete.*.

concepts.name: Partnership statements: appropriation, capital and current accounts
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Statement of profit or loss, appropriation account (partners' salaries, interest on capital, interest on drawings, share of residual profit or loss), fixed capital with current accounts and fluctuating capital accounts, partners' capital and current account ledgers and columnar layout, statement of financial position of a partnership; interest on partners' loans is an expense of the business, not an appropriation. Agreement and law are aacc.partnership.agreement.

concepts.name: The partnership agreement and the Partnership Act 1890
concepts.description: Cambridge only (AS Level). Cambridge detail: contents of a partnership agreement (profit-sharing ratio, salaries, interest on capital and drawings, loans, admission and retirement, disputes), advantages of having a written agreement; the default rules of the Partnership Act 1890 when there is none (equal sharing, no salaries, no interest on capital or drawings, 5% interest on loans) and their application to a dispute. ZIMSEC does not name the Act; Zimbabwean law is not examined.

concepts.name: Goodwill in partnership accounts
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Inherent (self-generated) against purchased goodwill; why goodwill arises on a change in a partnership; valuation methods as examiners use them (multiple of average profits or super-profits given in the question); opening a goodwill account, and creating then eliminating goodwill or writing it off without a goodwill account (sacrificing and gaining ratios); IAS 38 treatment of goodwill in outline. Revaluation of other assets is aacc.partnership.revaluation.

concepts.name: Revaluation of assets on a change in partnership
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Revaluation account: restating assets and liabilities to current values on a change, profit or loss on revaluation shared in the old ratio, ledger entries to partners' capital accounts, statement of financial position before and after, and revaluation with the assets remaining at old values (reversal entries). Combines with goodwill in exam questions; goodwill itself is aacc.partnership.goodwill.

concepts.name: Change of profit-sharing ratio and admission of a new partner
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Reasons for a change; effect of a changed ratio on profit shares (sacrifice and gain); admission of a new partner bringing in cash or assets; capital and current accounts; adjustments for goodwill and revaluation through the capital accounts; premium for goodwill; statement of financial position after admission. Retirement is aacc.partnership.retirement; mid-year changes are aacc.partnership.mid-year-changes.

concepts.name: Retirement or death of a partner
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Settling a retiring partner's capital and current account balances; goodwill and revaluation on retirement; payment by cash, transfer to a loan account or purchase of the share by the continuing partners; capital accounts of continuing partners; statement of financial position after retirement; death treated the same way with the estate as the creditor. Piecemeal realisation is not examined.

concepts.name: Partnership changes part-way through the accounting year
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Time-apportioning profit for the year before and after the change, preparing the appropriation account in two periods (different salaries, interest and ratios), interest on capital for part of a year, treatment of drawings, goodwill and revaluation on the date of change, partners' current accounts and the statement of financial position at the year end; reading the dates in the question carefully.

concepts.name: Dissolution of a partnership: realisation accounts
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Closing the books on dissolution: realisation account (assets sold, taken over by a partner or written off, expenses of realisation, profit or loss shared in the profit-sharing ratio), partners' capital accounts, bank account, settling creditors and discounts, loan accounts, deficiency of one partner's capital borne as the question states; the final cash distribution. Questions are not set on piecemeal realisation or on Garner v Murray.

concepts.name: Share capital, dividends and reserves
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Features of ordinary and preference shares (preference shares are ZIMSEC detail; Cambridge sets no questions on them), authorised, issued and called-up share capital, par (nominal) value, dividends (interim, final, proposed), capital reserves (share premium, revaluation reserve, capital redemption reserve) against revenue reserves (retained earnings, general reserve) and distributable against non-distributable reserves; the equity section of the statement of financial position.

concepts.name: Issue of shares at par or at a premium
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Ledger accounts for an issue of ordinary shares at par and at a premium (bank, share capital, share premium; applications and allotments when the question gives them), oversubscription and refunds, uses of share premium, effect on the statement of financial position and on gearing.

concepts.name: Bonus issues and rights issues
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Bonus (capitalisation) issue from reserves, rights issue to existing shareholders at a price below market (at par or at a premium), ledger entries for each, effect on share capital, reserves, market price and number of shares, which reserves may be used for a bonus (not the revaluation reserve in Cambridge questions), distinguishing the two issues, and advantages and disadvantages to the company and to shareholders; theoretical ex-rights price is not required.

concepts.name: Redemption and purchase of own shares; capital redemption reserve
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 6). ZIMSEC detail (Form 6): why a company redeems or buys back its shares, sources (a fresh issue of shares, distributable profits), accounting entries, creating a capital redemption reserve, effect on reserves and the statement of financial position; premium on redemption in outline. Not examined by Cambridge.

concepts.name: Loan notes and debentures: issue, redemption and convertible loan stock
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Issue of loan notes/debentures, interest paid and accrued, redemption at the end of the term, convertible loan stock converted into shares (ZIMSEC detail), secured against unsecured, extracts of the statement of financial position after issue or redemption, effect on gearing and cash flow; debentures against shares from the company's and investor's view (also aacc.capital.sources-of-capital).

concepts.name: Company statement of profit or loss
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Preparing the statement of profit or loss for a company in IAS 1 format (revenue, cost of sales, gross profit, distribution costs, administrative expenses, finance costs, profit before and after tax), directors' remuneration, income tax and its effect, interim and final dividends and transfers to reserves shown in the statement of changes in equity; ZIMSEC titles it statement of profit and loss and other comprehensive income (other comprehensive income includes revaluation gains).

concepts.name: Statement of changes in equity
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Columnar statement of changes in equity (share capital, share premium, revaluation reserve, general reserve, retained earnings) from opening balances, profit for the year, dividends, issues of shares at par or premium, bonus and rights issues, transfers to reserves, revaluation gain; reconciling closing balances to the statement of financial position.

concepts.name: Company statement of financial position
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). IAS 1 layout: non-current assets (property, plant and equipment, intangible assets), current assets, equity and reserves, non-current liabilities (loan notes), current liabilities (including tax payable, proposed dividends where the question gives them, and overdraft); preparation from a trial balance with adjustments, corrections and tax. Sole trader and partnership layouts are aacc.statements.sole-trader and aacc.partnership.accounts.

concepts.name: Notes to the financial statements and the schedule of non-current assets
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Schedule of non-current assets (cost or valuation, additions, disposals, depreciation for the year, accumulated depreciation, carrying amount), notes on accounting policies, share capital and reserves, dividends and borrowings, notes related to the statement of profit or loss and financial position under IAS 1 (internal-use statements, not for publication); reconciliation of the carrying amount.

concepts.name: Cash generated from operations (IAS 7 indirect method)
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Reconciling profit before tax to cash generated from operations: add back depreciation, loss and deduct profit on disposal, interest expense and income, changes in inventory, trade receivables and trade payables; reading the working-capital changes in the correct direction; calculating cash from operations from two statements of financial position and extra information; why profit and cash differ. The full statement is aacc.company.cash-flow-statement.

concepts.name: Statement of cash flows (IAS 7)
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Full statement of cash flows for a company: operating activities (indirect method), investing activities (purchase and sale of property, plant and equipment, interest and dividends received), financing activities (issue of shares, loan notes, repayments, dividends paid), interest and tax paid, net increase or decrease in cash and cash equivalents and reconciliation to the opening and closing cash and bank balances; ZIMSEC also asks for sole proprietors and partnerships (no tax, no share issues); interpreting the result.

concepts.name: Auditing, stewardship and directors' and auditors' reports
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Role and responsibilities of the auditor, external against internal audit, unqualified against qualified audit report (adverse opinion and disclaimer in outline), the contents of the auditor's report and directors' report in summary, stewardship (directors as stewards of shareholders' funds and their responsibilities), the true and fair view and why users rely on it, independence and threats to it. No named audit-standard numbers.

concepts.name: Business purchase: purchase consideration and goodwill
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Why businesses acquire or merge (growth, markets, skills, economies of scale); acquiring a business as a whole against buying individual assets; the purchase consideration (cash, shares, loan notes or a mixture); valuing net assets acquired and calculating goodwill (or a gain on a bargain purchase in outline); purchased goodwill and IAS 38 in outline.

concepts.name: Closing the books of a business taken over
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). The vendor's side: realisation account for a sole trader or partnership being taken over, assets transferred, liabilities settled or taken over, purchase consideration received in cash, shares or loan notes, profit or loss on realisation, closing the capital accounts of the owner or partners, final distribution of the consideration.

concepts.name: Recording a business purchase in the purchaser's books
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Journal entries and ledger accounts for a limited company acquiring a sole trader or partnership: business purchase account, assets and liabilities recorded at agreed values, goodwill, settlement by cash, issue of shares and loan notes (par or premium); effect on the share capital, share premium and reserves.

concepts.name: Mergers and statements of financial position after a purchase or merger
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Merger of two or more sole traders into a partnership or company, of a sole trader with an existing partnership into a new partnership, and a company absorbing a partnership; the opening statement of financial position of the new or enlarged business, statements of profit or loss after acquisition; Cambridge detail: advantages and disadvantages of an acquisition or merger. Consolidated accounts are not examined.

concepts.name: Statement of affairs and profit from the accounting equation
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Drawing up a statement of affairs at an opening or closing date, calculating opening and closing capital, profit or loss for the year from the change in capital (closing capital less opening capital plus drawings less capital introduced), the accounting equation used with incomplete records, and the limitations of this method.

concepts.name: Missing figures: ledger accounts, margin and mark-up
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Reconstructing missing amounts with total accounts (sales, purchases, receivables, payables), cash and bank summaries, cash stolen or lost, accruals and prepayments, drawings; using gross profit margin and mark-up percentages to find sales, purchases or cost of sales; profit estimation; inventory lost by fire or theft; each figure traced to the working that produced it. Margin and mark-up as ratios are in aacc.ratios.profitability.

concepts.name: Final accounts from incomplete records
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge AS Level). Preparing the statement of profit or loss and statement of financial position of a trading or service business from incomplete records after reconstructing the missing figures, for a sole trader and for a partnership (appropriation); allowance for irrecoverable debts, depreciation and accruals included; checking that the statement of financial position balances.

concepts.name: Receipts and payments account and the accumulated fund
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Receipts and payments account (cash summary: what it shows and does not show), converting it to an income and expenditure account, opening statement of affairs, defining and calculating the accumulated fund (net assets at the start of the year), incomplete-records style questions for a club; the receipts and payments account is Cambridge detail (ZIMSEC asks for the accumulated fund).

concepts.name: Subscriptions: advance, arrears and the subscriptions account
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Subscriptions account with arrears and advance at both year ends, writing off irrecoverable subscriptions, subscriptions income for the year, subscriptions received for an earlier or later period, effect on the statement of financial position (current assets: arrears; current liabilities: advance), and the matching of income to the year.

concepts.name: Trading and income-generating activities of clubs
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Income statements for activities such as the bar, a canteen, dinner dances, raffles and a tuck shop (revenue less cost of sales and direct expenses, profit or loss transferred to the income and expenditure account), cost of sales from opening and closing inventory and payments, accruals; preparing from incomplete information.

concepts.name: Income and expenditure account and the club's statement of financial position
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Income and expenditure account (surplus or deficit) with subscriptions, activity profits, donations, life membership fees (spread over time or taken to the accumulated fund) and sundry income against expenses and depreciation; adjustments (accruals, prepayments, depreciation, irrecoverable subscriptions); the statement of financial position with the accumulated fund; accounting treatment of different types of donation (revenue, capital, specific purpose).

concepts.name: Sources of income and fundraising for non-profit organisations
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Sources of income of clubs and societies (subscriptions, entrance fees, donations, grants, fundraising events, trading activities, investments), advantages and disadvantages of each, evaluating methods of fundraising and sources of finance for a stated purpose and recommending one; Zimbabwean examples (school clubs, savings clubs, churches, sports clubs). No calculations beyond simple comparisons.

concepts.name: The manufacturing account
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Direct materials, direct labour, direct expenses and prime cost, factory overheads, work in progress (opening and closing), cost of production, cost per unit; direct against indirect expenses and apportionment of shared expenses between factory and office; classification of manufacturing costs; the manufacturing account for a small to medium or large business.

concepts.name: Manufacturing profit and the provision for unrealised profit
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Transferring finished goods to the trading account at cost or at market value; manufacturing (factory) profit; why a business accounts for it (to compare internal cost with market price); the provision for unrealised profit in closing inventory, the increase or decrease in the provision each year, and its place in the statement of profit or loss and statement of financial position.

concepts.name: Final accounts of a manufacturing business
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 5; Cambridge A Level only). Complete set for a manufacturing business: manufacturing account, statement of profit or loss (with raw materials, work in progress and finished goods inventories) and statement of financial position (inventories of raw materials, WIP and finished goods separately), with adjustments, for a sole trader and a company (ZIMSEC: small to medium and large firms).

concepts.name: Apportioning expenses and income to departments
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). ZIMSEC detail: bases of apportionment (floor area, number of employees, sales, purchases, cost of sales, asset values, usage), common expenses against departmental expenses, ancillary income such as commission or rent, choosing a fair basis, calculating each department's share from information given. Not examined by Cambridge.

concepts.name: Departmental statements of profit or loss and financial position
concepts.description: ZIMSEC only (Form 5). ZIMSEC detail: departmental trading and profit or loss columns (gross profit and net profit per department), combined totals, evaluating departments (percentage margins, whether to close a loss-making department), and the single statement of financial position. Not examined by Cambridge.

concepts.name: IAS 1 Presentation of financial statements and IAS 2 Inventories
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Purpose and main provisions of IAS 1 (complete set of statements, fair presentation, going concern, accruals, consistency, materiality and aggregation, offsetting, comparative information, current and non-current classification, minimum line items) and IAS 2 (lower of cost and net realisable value, cost formulae, disclosure); applying them to a set of statements. Calculations are in aacc.valuation.inventory.

concepts.name: IAS 8 Accounting policies, estimates and errors; IAS 10 Events after the reporting period
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). IAS 8: selecting accounting policies, changes in policy (retrospective), changes in accounting estimates (prospective), correcting material prior-period errors; IAS 10: adjusting and non-adjusting events after the reporting period and the disclosure of the latter, with classification of described events and their effect on figures.

concepts.name: IAS 16 Property, plant and equipment; IAS 36 Impairment; IAS 38 Intangible assets
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). IAS 16 recognition, measurement, depreciation and disclosure (calculations are aacc.valuation.nca-models); IAS 36 impairment: recoverable amount (higher of fair value less costs of disposal and value in use), when to test, recognising an impairment loss; IAS 38 intangible assets: recognition criteria, internally generated goodwill not recognised, research against development expenditure, amortisation.

concepts.name: IAS 37 Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only). Cambridge detail (A Level): when a provision is recognised (present obligation, probable outflow, reliable estimate), contingent liabilities (disclosed, not recognised) and contingent assets, treatment of a described event (legal claim, warranty, restructuring), and the entries for a provision. Not in the ZIMSEC list of standards.

concepts.name: Profitability ratios
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Gross profit margin, mark-up, profit margin (net profit margin), return on capital employed (profit from operations / capital employed, capital employed = issued shares + reserves + non-current liabilities) and the expenses-to-revenue and operating-expenses-to-revenue ratios with the formulae printed in the Cambridge appendix; ZIMSEC detail: return on assets and return on equity; comparing two years or two businesses and explaining the movement (price, volume, cost control).

concepts.name: Liquidity ratios
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Current ratio and acid test (quick) ratio, expressed as x : 1, what a high or low ratio means, levels depend on the industry, improving liquidity (collecting receivables, stretching payables, reducing inventory, raising finance), window dressing in outline, overtrading; comparing businesses.

concepts.name: Efficiency and resource-utilisation ratios
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Inventory turnover in days and times, trade receivables and trade payables turnover in days, non-current asset turnover; ZIMSEC detail: total assets, current assets and capital employed turnover; interpreting changes (credit control, supplier terms, stock control); average against year-end figures when the question states. The working capital cycle is aacc.ratios.solvency-gearing.

concepts.name: Solvency, gearing and the working capital cycle
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Gearing (fixed cost capital / total capital), interest cover; ZIMSEC detail: debt to equity ratio; Cambridge A Level: working capital cycle (days) and net working assets to revenue; interpreting risk for shareholders and lenders, the effect of high gearing in good and bad years, and ways to change gearing.

concepts.name: Investment (stock exchange) ratios
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Earnings per share, price/earnings ratio, dividend per share, dividend yield, dividend cover (both boards); ZIMSEC detail: earnings yield; what each tells an investor, comparing companies and years, effect of bonus and rights issues on earnings per share in outline, limits of the ratios; calculations use the printed formulae with ordinary-share figures only.

concepts.name: Interpreting ratios, interrelationships and limitations
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Writing a structured analysis of profitability, liquidity and efficiency for two years or two businesses, linking ratios (margin and turnover to ROCE, receivables days to liquidity, gearing to profit), recommendations to stakeholders and measures to improve performance, limitations of accounting information and ratios (historical, window dressing, different policies, inflation, non-financial factors, no standard benchmark); communicating the result in a report.

concepts.name: Cost terminology and the purposes of cost accounting
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Cost, costing, cost coding, cost unit, cost centre, direct and indirect costs, period and product costs, relevant and irrelevant costs, opportunity costs and sunk costs; the purposes of cost accounting (cost control, pricing, inventory valuation, decisions); cost accounting against management accounting and against financial accounting; the elements of cost (material, labour, expenses). Behaviour is aacc.cost.behaviour.

concepts.name: Cost behaviour: fixed, variable, semi-variable and stepped costs
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Fixed, variable, semi-variable (semi-fixed) and stepped costs, graphs described in words and as tables of cost against activity, separating a semi-variable cost into fixed and variable parts with the high-low method, the relevant range, total against unit cost behaviour, effect on unit cost of changing output.

concepts.name: Accounting for materials and labour; just in time
concepts.description: Cambridge only (AS Level). Cambridge detail: accounting for material costs (purchase, issue, returns, stores ledger, inventory levels) and labour costs (time and piece rates, overtime, idle time, labour cost per unit, gross-to-net wages); direct and indirect labour and materials; the principles, benefits and risks of just-in-time (JIT) inventory management. Valuation formulae are aacc.valuation.inventory.

concepts.name: Overhead allocation, apportionment and reapportionment
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Allocation of costs to cost centres, apportionment of shared overheads on suitable bases (floor area, value of assets, employees, machine hours), reapportioning service department costs to production departments, the overhead analysis sheet, ZIMSEC allotment; production and service departments.

concepts.name: Overhead absorption rates
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Choice of absorption basis (direct labour hours, machine hours, direct labour cost, prime cost, units), calculating pre-determined overhead absorption rates for each cost centre or for the factory, absorbing overheads into units, jobs or batches, the effect of the basis on unit cost.

concepts.name: Over- and under-absorption of overheads
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Calculating over- or under-absorbed overheads (absorbed less actual), causes (activity higher or lower than budget, overhead spending different from budget), the overhead control account entries, the adjustment to profit in absorption costing, interpreting the amount.

concepts.name: Absorption costing statements and profit; uses and limitations
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Preparing cost statements and profit statements using absorption costing (production and non-production overheads, opening and closing inventory valued at full cost, effect of inventory change on profit), selling price on a cost-plus basis; uses and limitations of absorption costing, non-financial factors, usefulness of absorption cost data to decision-making.

concepts.name: Marginal costing: contribution and profit statements
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Contribution per unit and in total, marginal cost statements and profit statements with inventory valued at variable production cost, fixed costs written off in the period, the effect of changing sales and production; uses and limitations of marginal costing. Contribution to sales ratio is applied in aacc.cost.break-even.

concepts.name: Marginal against absorption costing: reconciling the profits
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Differences between marginal and absorption costing, why profits differ when inventory changes (fixed overheads in inventory), reconciling the profit under the two methods (change in inventory x fixed overhead absorption rate per unit) with rising, falling and constant inventory, which method gives the higher profit and why.

concepts.name: Break-even analysis and cost-volume-profit calculations
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Break-even point in units and revenue, contribution to sales ratio, margin of safety (units, revenue, percentage), output or sales needed for a target profit, effect of changes in price, cost and mix; interpreting a break-even chart (a chart is not drawn in Cambridge examinations); assumptions and limitations of break-even analysis.

concepts.name: Short-run decisions and cost-volume-profit data
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Make-or-buy, accepting a special order, closing a business unit or product, limiting-factor decisions (contribution per scarce resource), setting a target profit and pricing, choosing between options using relevant costs and contribution; non-financial factors (quality, jobs, reputation, supplier reliability, ethics); advantages and limitations of cost-volume-profit analysis and recommendations supported by data.

concepts.name: Job, batch and unit costing
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge AS Level). Cost sheets: prime cost of a job or batch, absorbing overheads into a job, total cost, adding a profit margin or mark-up to find the selling price, cost per unit of a batch, job and batch costing in service businesses, unit costing for a single product; contract and process costing are not examined.

concepts.name: Activity based costing (ABC)
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only). Cambridge detail (A Level): activities and cost drivers, cost pools, calculating a cost-driver rate, allocating overheads to products by their use of activities, total and unit cost and selling price under ABC, comparing with traditional absorption (labour-hour) costing and the effect on cost and profit, uses and limitations of ABC, decisions based on ABC data.

concepts.name: Standard costing: meaning, standards and uses
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). What standard costing is, setting standard costs for materials, labour and overheads, types of standard (ideal, attainable, current, basic), the standard cost card, advantages and disadvantages of a standard costing system, how standard costing aids planning, control and performance improvement.

concepts.name: Direct material and direct labour variances
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Direct material price and usage variances, direct labour rate and efficiency variances (ZIMSEC material and labour variances), total direct cost variance, favourable and adverse labelling, calculations from actual and standard data, material price at the point of purchase or usage as the question states.

concepts.name: Sales price and sales volume variances
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Sales price variance and sales volume (profit) variance at standard profit or contribution as the question states, favourable and adverse, causes (discounting, competition, demand) and their link to production variances.

concepts.name: Fixed overhead variances
concepts.description: Cambridge only (A Level only). Cambridge detail (A Level): fixed overhead expenditure and volume variances, and the volume variance split into capacity and efficiency sub-variances, with budgeted and absorbed overheads; favourable and adverse. ZIMSEC states that questions on overhead variances will not be set.

concepts.name: Analysing variances and reconciling standard to actual
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Reconciling standard cost or budgeted profit with actual cost or profit by listing the variances, causes of favourable and adverse variances (quality of material, wage grades, training, price changes, machine breakdowns) and the relationships between them (cheaper materials causing adverse usage), management action, non-financial factors.

concepts.name: Budgetary control: purpose, advantages and behavioural aspects
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Why organisations budget (planning, control, co-ordination, communication, motivation, authorisation), advantages and disadvantages of budgetary control, budgeting with spreadsheets, behavioural aspects (targets, participation, incentives, slack, motivation), limiting (principal budget) factors and their effect, the master budget in outline.

concepts.name: Sales, production, purchases, labour and working-capital budgets
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Preparing the sales budget, production budget (units with inventory changes), purchases budget (materials, inventory), labour budget, and trade receivables and trade payables budgets from the data, using limiting factors to adjust a budget, checking that budgets agree.

concepts.name: The cash budget
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Preparing a monthly cash budget from sales, purchases, expenses, credit terms, discounts, drawings, loans, capital expenditure and dividends, opening and closing cash balances, non-cash items excluded, interpreting the result and recommending action for a deficit or surplus (overdraft, delaying payments, leasing, short-term investment).

concepts.name: Master budget: budgeted profit and financial position
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Combining operating budgets into a master budget: budgeted statement of profit or loss and statement of financial position for the period from the opening statement of financial position, checking that the budgeted statement balances; using the master budget to assess a plan.

concepts.name: Flexible budgets and comparing budget with actual
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Fixed against flexible (flexed) budgets, benefits of flexing, preparing a flexible budget statement for actual activity using fixed, variable and semi-variable costs, causes of differences between actual and flexed data, reconciling the flexed budgeted cost of production with actual cost of production, and the flexed budgeted profit with actual profit; interpreting and recommending action.

concepts.name: Payback period and accounting rate of return
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Net cash inflows and outflows of a project, payback period in years and months (even and uneven inflows), accounting rate of return = average profit / average investment x 100 (Cambridge formula; residual values are not set in Cambridge questions), accept/reject criteria, advantages and disadvantages of each; discounted payback is not examined.

concepts.name: Net present value and internal rate of return
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Time value of money, discount factors from a table supplied in the question, present value of cash flows, net present value and decision rule, internal rate of return by interpolation between two discount rates, the cost of capital as the cut-off; advantages and disadvantages against payback and ARR.

concepts.name: Evaluating investment projects and making recommendations
concepts.description: Both boards (ZIMSEC Form 6; Cambridge A Level only). Comparing projects with several techniques at once, choosing between mutually exclusive projects when techniques disagree, the difference between accounting profits and cash flows, risk and uncertainty in the forecasts, non-financial factors (employment, environment, strategy, reputation), a reasoned recommendation using supporting data.
